source_title: Ray Nicholson Reveals He Nearly Lost His Arm to a Serious Infection Before Becoming an Actor (Exclusive) - People.com
source_excerpt:
Ray Nicholson tells PEOPLE how a life-threatening infection ended his high school football career and inspired him to pursue acting
Tommy McArdle is a Writer-Reporter on the Movies team at PEOPLE. He joined the brand in 2022.
Ray Nicholson tells PEOPLE how an infection ended his high school football career — and what it meant to return to the field for his new movie, The Mosquito Bowl
Nicholson stars alongside Tom Francis, Bill Skarsgård and Nicholas Galitzine in the World War II drama
The Mosquito Bowl hits theaters Oct. 30 before streaming on Netflix Nov. 25
Ray Nicholson got to relive his high school football days in his new movie, The Mosquito Bowl . As it turns out, his experience on the field helped set him on the path toward an acting career.
Speaking with PEOPLE alongside costar Tom Francis, Nicholson, 34, reflects on the impact football had on his life growing up.
“I really loved it. I knew I wasn’t good enough to be a pro,” he says. “I worked out with guys that were good enough to be a pro, and I think I had a really big heart, but I just didn’t have the physical gifts that other people had.”
“But I definitely had the work ethic, so I thought that I was gonna be a Jerry Maguire,” he adds, referencing Tom Cruise’s sports agent character in the 1996 movie of the same name.
Ray, the son of Jack Nicholson and actress Rebecca Broussard, played running back and linebacker in high school, according to the high school sports website MaxPreps . But his football career came to an abrupt end after he developed a serious infection.
“My last football game, I got staph infection that turned into MRSA [methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus ],” he recalls. “My arm got so swollen up, they literally drew a line on my arm and were like, ‘If the infection gets past here, we have to cut off your arm.’ I lost, like, 50 pounds in a week, almost in a semi-coma, and I kind of came out of that being like, ‘Oh my God, I, I want to be an actor.’”
Ray previously told PEOPLE that he had long resisted pursuing a career in show business, at one point envisioning a future as a sports agent. Now, he says his brush with a potentially life-altering illness helped him embrace what he had wanted to do all along.
“This is the thing that I’ve always wanted to do, but I’ve been afraid to do, and football was the first thing that held me up and gave my life meaning,” he says.
Ray made his onscreen debut in the 2006 sports comedy The Benchwarmers , but he didn’t begin pursuing acting in earnest until 2018’s The Outsider . His breakout came in 2024 with movies including Smile 2 . In The Mosquito Bowl , he portrays real-life 1940s college football star Tony Butkovich, who went from being a standout running back at Purdue University to serving as a U.S. Marine during World War II.
Based on the 2022 nonfiction book Mosquito Bowl: A Game of Life and Death in World War II , the movie follows four college football players who go on to serve in the Pacific Theater during World War II. The story culminates in a real-life football game played by U.S. Marines stationed on the island of Guadalcanal on Dec. 24, 1944.
The role gave Nicholson a chance to put his football skills to use again as an adult. It also allowed him to help teach his costars, including Francis, 27, Bill Skarsgård and Nicholas Galitzine — none of whom grew up in the U.S. — the ins and outs of American football.
“This job was a dream. It was a complete dream, to be able to be there, to look at a character through the prism of football, and then to be of service to my castmates. It was really a dream come true,” Ray says.
Tony Award nominee Francis, who hails from England, says he quickly bonded with Nicholson and their other costars during a monthlong football and military training camp in Australia before filming began. Francis leaned on Nicholson’s firsthand knowledge of American football to help him convincingly portray a lifelong player in the new movie.
“Ray was instrumental in helping us through that. On the way to every practice, on the way back from every practice, on the weekends, we’d watch games,” he says. “He would help me through plays, teach me the rules, teach me the differences between playing football then and now.”
“You just kinda have to do it. I feel like I’m quite a practical person and Ray was very helpful at being able to help me do it,” Francis adds.
The Mosquito Bowl is in theaters Oct. 30. The movie begins streaming on Netflix Nov. 25.
